claim: Local circadian clocks are active in most cells of our body.
source: Local circadian clocks are active in most cells of our body.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific knowledge about circadian clocks.

claim: Mortality by endotoxic (LPS) shock is highly time-of-day dependent.
source: Mortality by endotoxic (LPS) shock is highly time-of-day dependent and local circadian immune function such as the cytokine burst after LPS challenge has been assumed to be causal for the large differences in survival.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations in the introduction and by experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Local circadian immune function such as the cytokine burst after LPS challenge has been assumed to be causal for the large differences in survival.
source: Mortality by endotoxic (LPS) shock is highly time-of-day dependent and local circadian immune function such as the cytokine burst after LPS challenge has been assumed to be causal for the large differences in survival.
evidence: This represents a hypothesis based on prior literature that the authors are testing.

claim: Mice in constant darkness (DD) show a threefold increased susceptibility to LPS as compared to mice in light-dark conditions.
source: Strikingly, mice in constant darkness (DD) show a threefold increased susceptibility to LPS as compared to mice in light-dark conditions.
evidence: This is directly supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1.

claim: Mortality by endotoxic shock as a function of circadian time is independent of light-dark cycles.
source: Mortality by endotoxic shock as a function of circadian time is independent of light-dark cycles as well as myeloid CLOCK or BMAL1 as demonstrated in conditional knockout mice.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from mice in DD conditions showing circadian mortality patterns.

claim: Mortality by endotoxic shock as a function of circadian time is independent of myeloid CLOCK.
source: Mortality by endotoxic shock as a function of circadian time is independent of light-dark cycles as well as myeloid CLOCK or BMAL1 as demonstrated in conditional knockout mice.
evidence: This is demonstrated by experiments with myClock-KO mice showing persistent circadian mortality patterns.

claim: Mortality by endotoxic shock as a function of circadian time is independent of myeloid BMAL1.
source: Mortality by endotoxic shock as a function of circadian time is independent of light-dark cycles as well as myeloid CLOCK or BMAL1 as demonstrated in conditional knockout mice.
evidence: This is demonstrated by experiments with myBmal-KO mice showing persistent circadian mortality patterns.

claim: Despite the lack of a myeloid clock, mice still show rhythmic patterns of pro- and anti-inflammatory cytokines such as TNFα, MCP-1, IL-18, and IL-10 in peripheral blood.
source: Unexpectedly, despite the lack of a myeloid clock these mice still show rhythmic patterns of pro- and anti-inflammatory cytokines such as TNFα, MCP-1, IL-18, and IL-10 in peripheral blood as well as time-of-day and site-dependent traffic of myeloid cells.
evidence: This is supported by cytokine measurements in myClock-KO mice shown in Figure 4.

claim: Despite the lack of a myeloid clock, mice still show time-of-day and site-dependent traffic of myeloid cells.
source: Unexpectedly, despite the lack of a myeloid clock these mice still show rhythmic patterns of pro- and anti-inflammatory cytokines such as TNFα, MCP-1, IL-18, and IL-10 in peripheral blood as well as time-of-day and site-dependent traffic of myeloid cells.
evidence: This is supported by FACS analysis of immune cell populations shown in Figure 5.

claim: Systemic time-cues are sufficient to orchestrate innate immune response to LPS by driving immune functions such as cell trafficking and cytokine expression.
source: We speculate that systemic time-cues are sufficient to orchestrate innate immune response to LPS by driving immune functions such as cell trafficking and cytokine expression.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the experimental findings.

claim: Many parameters and functions of the immune system display diurnal patterns in humans.
source: In humans, many parameters and functions of the immune system display diurnal patterns (Scheiermann et al., 2013), which impact on disease severity and symptoms (Druzd et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Diurnal patterns of immune function impact on disease severity and symptoms.
source: In humans, many parameters and functions of the immune system display diurnal patterns (Scheiermann et al., 2013), which impact on disease severity and symptoms (Druzd et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: The circadian clock in mammals is organized in a hierarchical manner.
source: In mammals, this clock is organized in a hierarchical manner: a central pacemaker in the brain synchronized to environmental light-dark cycles via the eyes and peripheral clocks receiving and integrating central as well as peripheral (e.g. metabolic) time information.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the mammalian circadian system.

claim: A central pacemaker in the brain is synchronized to environmental light-dark cycles via the eyes.
source: In mammals, this clock is organized in a hierarchical manner: a central pacemaker in the brain synchronized to environmental light-dark cycles via the eyes and peripheral clocks receiving and integrating central as well as peripheral (e.g. metabolic) time information.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the mammalian circadian system.

claim: Peripheral clocks receive and integrate central as well as peripheral (e.g. metabolic) time information.
source: In mammals, this clock is organized in a hierarchical manner: a central pacemaker in the brain synchronized to environmental light-dark cycles via the eyes and peripheral clocks receiving and integrating central as well as peripheral (e.g. metabolic) time information.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the mammalian circadian system.

claim: Central and peripheral clocks are essentially identical in their molecular makeup.
source: Both central and peripheral clocks are essentially identical in their molecular makeup: Core transcription factors form a negative feedback loop consisting of the activators, CLOCK and BMAL1, and the repressors, PERs and CRYs.
evidence: This is established knowledge about circadian clock molecular mechanisms.

claim: Core transcription factors form a negative feedback loop consisting of the activators, CLOCK and BMAL1, and the repressors, PERs and CRYs.
source: Both central and peripheral clocks are essentially identical in their molecular makeup: Core transcription factors form a negative feedback loop consisting of the activators, CLOCK and BMAL1, and the repressors, PERs and CRYs.
evidence: This is established knowledge about circadian clock molecular mechanisms.

claim: Additional feedback loops and regulatory factors amplify, stabilize and fine-tune the cell intrinsic molecular oscillator to achieve an about 24 hr (circadian) periodicity of cell- and tissue-specific clock output functions.
source: Additional feedback loops and regulatory factors amplify, stabilize and fine-tune the cell intrinsic molecular oscillator to achieve an about 24 hr (circadian) periodicity of cell- and tissue-specific clock output functions (Bass and Lazar, 2016).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: Circadian patterns of various immune-functions have been reported in mice.
source: Circadian patterns of various immune-functions have been reported in mice (Scheiermann et al., 2013) and other species (Haus and Smolensky, 1999; Wang et al., 2011; Lee and Edery, 2008) including cytokine response to bacterial endotoxin and pathogens, white blood cell traffic (Méndez-Ferrer et al., 2008; Scheiermann et al., 2012; Casanova-Acebes et al., 2013) and natural killer cell activity (Arjona and Sarkar, 2006).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: Circadian patterns of various immune-functions have been reported in other species.
source: Circadian patterns of various immune-functions have been reported in mice (Scheiermann et al., 2013) and other species (Haus and Smolensky, 1999; Wang et al., 2011; Lee and Edery, 2008) including cytokine response to bacterial endotoxin and pathogens, white blood cell traffic (Méndez-Ferrer et al., 2008; Scheiermann et al., 2012; Casanova-Acebes et al., 2013) and natural killer cell activity (Arjona and Sarkar, 2006).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: Cell-intrinsic clocks have been described for many leukocyte subsets of lymphoid as well as myeloid origin, including monocytes/macrophages.
source: Cell-intrinsic clocks have been described for many leukocyte subsets of lymphoid as well as myeloid origin, including monocytes/macrophages (Keller et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: Immune-cell intrinsic clocks have been connected to cell-type specific output function such as the TNFα response to LPS in macrophages.
source: Furthermore, immune-cell intrinsic clocks have been connected to cell-type specific output function such as the TNFα response to LPS in macrophages (Keller et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: Sepsis is a severe life threatening condition with more than 31 million incidences per year worldwide.
source: Sepsis is a severe life threatening condition with more than 31 million incidences per year worldwide (Fleischmann et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citation to epidemiological data.

claim: Mouse models of sepsis show a strong time-of-day dependency in mortality rate when challenged at different times of the day.
source: Mouse models of sepsis show a strong time-of-day dependency in mortality rate when challenged at different times of the day (Halberg et al., 1960; Feigin et al., 1969; Feigin et al., 1972; Hrushesky et al., 1994; Deng et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: Most studies agree about the times of highest (around Zeitgeber time [ZT]8 - that is, 8 hr past lights on) or lowest (around ZT20) mortality across different animal models and investigators.
source: Most studies agree about the times of highest (around Zeitgeber time [ZT]8 - that is, 8 hr past lights on) or lowest (around ZT20) mortality across different animal models and investigators (Halberg et al., 1960; Hrushesky et al., 1994; Feigin et al., 1969; Feigin et al., 1972).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: The fatal cascade in the pathomechanism of endotoxic shock is initiated by critical doses of LPS recognized by CD14/TLR4-bearing cells, mainly monocytes and macrophages as well as the activation of the complement system.
source: The fatal cascade in the pathomechanism of endotoxic shock is initiated by critical doses of LPS recognized by CD14/TLR4-bearing cells, mainly monocytes and macrophages as well as the activation of the complement system.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the pathophysiology of endotoxic shock.

claim: Activation of the innate immune system triggers a massive release of pro-inflammatory cytokines and feeds into a self amplifying loop involving the cytokine release of not only newly recruited leukocytes but also endothelial and other cells.
source: This activation of the innate immune system triggers a massive release of pro-inflammatory cytokines and feeds into a self amplifying loop involving the cytokine release of not only newly recruited leukocytes but also endothelial and other cells (Hotchkiss et al., 2016).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation.

claim: Activation of the coagulation system in endothelial cells, platelets, and plasma as well as increasing endothelial barrier dysfunction promote disseminated intra-vascular coagulation, blood pressure decompensation and final multi-organ dysfunction.
source: As a consequence, activation of the coagulation system in endothelial cells, platelets, and plasma as well as increasing endothelial barrier dysfunction promote disseminated intra-vascular coagulation, blood pressure decompensation and final multi-organ dysfunction (McConnell and Coopersmith, 2016; Hotchkiss et al., 2016).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Peripheral blood cytokine levels triggered by bacterial endotoxin depend on time-of-day despite a functional clock knockout in myeloid cells.
source: We show that peripheral blood cytokine levels as well as mortality triggered by bacterial endotoxin depend on time-of-day despite a functional clock knockout in myeloid cells.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from myClock-KO mice shown in Figure 4.

claim: Mortality triggered by bacterial endotoxin depends on time-of-day despite a functional clock knockout in myeloid cells.
source: We show that peripheral blood cytokine levels as well as mortality triggered by bacterial endotoxin depend on time-of-day despite a functional clock knockout in myeloid cells.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from myClock-KO and myBmal-KO mice shown in Figures 2 and 3.

claim: Diurnal patterns of LPS-induced mortality (endotoxic shock) have been reported numerous times in different laboratory mouse strains.
source: Diurnal patterns of LPS-induced mortality (endotoxic shock) have been reported numerous times in different laboratory mouse strains (Halberg et al., 1960; Marpegan et al., 2009; Scheiermann et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: Survival of mice housed in LD was dependent on the time of LPS injection, being highest during the light phase and lowest at night.
source: As expected from previous reports, survival of mice housed in LD was dependent on the time of LPS injection, being highest during the light phase and lowest at night (Figure 1A, Figure 1—figure supplement 1A–C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Mice challenged 1 day after transfer in constant darkness using the same dose showed a more than 60% increase in overall mortality compared to mice kept in LD.
source: Surprisingly, mice challenged 1 day after transfer in constant darkness using the same dose showed a more than 60% increase in overall mortality compared to mice kept in LD (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: Time-of-day-dependent differences in mortality were much less pronounced under DD conditions.
source: Furthermore, time-of-day-dependent differences in mortality were much less pronounced under these conditions.
evidence: This is inferred from the data shown in Figure 1A comparing LD and DD conditions.

claim: Mice in DD showed a threefold increased susceptibility to LPS as similar doses of LPS result in largely different mortality rates in LD vs. DD (e.g. LD, 15 mg/kg LPS, 9% mortality vs DD, 13 mg/kg LPS, 67% mortality).
source: As suspected, mice in DD showed a threefold increased susceptibility to LPS as similar doses of LPS result in largely different mortality rates in LD vs. DD (e.g. LD, 15 mg/kg LPS, 9% mortality vs DD, 13 mg/kg LPS, 67% mortality).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Diurnal/circadian patterns in mortality rate were observed in LD (p-value=0.06) as well as in DD conditions (p-value=0.001).
source: This revealed diurnal/circadian patterns in mortality rate in LD (p-value=0.06) as well as in DD conditions (p-value=0.001) (Figure 1C) demonstrating that the circadian system controls susceptibility to LPS.
evidence: This is supported by statistical analysis of experimental data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: The circadian system controls susceptibility to LPS.
source: This revealed diurnal/circadian patterns in mortality rate in LD (p-value=0.06) as well as in DD conditions (p-value=0.001) (Figure 1C) demonstrating that the circadian system controls susceptibility to LPS.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation of circadian patterns in mortality in DD conditions.

claim: The susceptibility to LPS is overall increased in constant darkness.
source: In addition, this susceptibility is overall increased in constant darkness (Figure 1A,B and Figure 1—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in multiple figures.

claim: Cells in the immune system harbor self-sustained circadian oscillators, which shape immune functions in a circadian manner.
source: We and others have recently found that cells in the immune system harbor self-sustained circadian oscillators, which shape immune functions in a circadian manner (Keller et al., 2009; Hayashi et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Pro-inflammatory responses in murine ex vivo macrophage culture are controlled by cell-intrinsic clocks and are most prominent during the day and lowest during the activity phase.
source: Pro-inflammatory responses in murine ex vivo macrophage culture (Keller et al., 2009; Bellet et al., 2013) are controlled by cell-intrinsic clocks and are most prominent during the day and lowest during the activity phase.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Pro-inflammatory cytokines such as TNFα, IL-1α/β, IL-6, IL-18 as well as MCP-1 have been linked to the pathomechanism of endotoxic shock.
source: Furthermore, pro-inflammatory cytokines such as TNFα, IL-1α/β, IL-6, IL-18 as well as MCP-1 have been linked to the pathomechanism of endotoxic shock (Xing et al., 1998; Andrews et al., 2011; Gomes et al., 2006; Li et al., 1995; Marino et al., 1997).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: Plasma of mice collected 2 hr after administration of half-lethal doses of LPS exhibited an up to twofold time-of-day difference in absolute cytokine concentrations.
source: Indeed, plasma of mice collected 2 hr after administration of half-lethal doses of LPS (either in LD [30 mg/kg] or DD [13 mg/kg] conditions at various times during the day), exhibited an up to twofold time-of-day difference in absolute cytokine concentrations.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: In animals kept in LD, TNFα showed highest levels around ZT8.
source: In animals kept in LD, TNFα showed highest levels around ZT8, IL-18 levels peaked at ZT18 and IL-12p40 as well as the anti-inflammatory cytokine IL-10 had their peak-time around ZT14 (Figure 1D and Figure 1—figure supplement 1E; for amplitude and phase information as determined by sine fit see Figure 1E and Figure 1—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: In animals kept in LD, IL-18 levels peaked at ZT18.
source: In animals kept in LD, TNFα showed highest levels around ZT8, IL-18 levels peaked at ZT18 and IL-12p40 as well as the anti-inflammatory cytokine IL-10 had their peak-time around ZT14 (Figure 1D and Figure 1—figure supplement 1E; for amplitude and phase information as determined by sine fit see Figure 1E and Figure 1—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: In animals kept in LD, IL-12p40 as well as the anti-inflammatory cytokine IL-10 had their peak-time around ZT14.
source: In animals kept in LD, TNFα showed highest levels around ZT8, IL-18 levels peaked at ZT18 and IL-12p40 as well as the anti-inflammatory cytokine IL-10 had their peak-time around ZT14 (Figure 1D and Figure 1—figure supplement 1E; for amplitude and phase information as determined by sine fit see Figure 1E and Figure 1—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Cytokine profiles from DD mice differed substantially from LD profiles.
source: Interestingly, cytokine profiles from DD mice differed substantially from LD profiles: the peak-times of IL-12p40 was phase-advanced by 6 hr, CXCL5 completely reversed its phase, whereas IL-18 remained expressed predominantly in the night.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D and 1E.

claim: The peak-times of IL-12p40 was phase-advanced by 6 hr in DD compared to LD.
source: Interestingly, cytokine profiles from DD mice differed substantially from LD profiles: the peak-times of IL-12p40 was phase-advanced by 6 hr, CXCL5 completely reversed its phase, whereas IL-18 remained expressed predominantly in the night.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: CXCL5 completely reversed its phase in DD compared to LD.
source: Interestingly, cytokine profiles from DD mice differed substantially from LD profiles: the peak-times of IL-12p40 was phase-advanced by 6 hr, CXCL5 completely reversed its phase, whereas IL-18 remained expressed predominantly in the night.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: IL-18 remained expressed predominantly in the night in both LD and DD conditions.
source: Interestingly, cytokine profiles from DD mice differed substantially from LD profiles: the peak-times of IL-12p40 was phase-advanced by 6 hr, CXCL5 completely reversed its phase, whereas IL-18 remained expressed predominantly in the night.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: Cytokine profiles of LPS-challenged mice parallel endotoxic shock-induced mortality patterns.
source: Taken together, cytokine profiles of LPS-challenged mice parallel endotoxic shock-induced mortality patterns, although most circadian cytokines show variable phase relations between free-running and entrained conditions (Figure 1E).
evidence: This is inferred from comparison of cytokine and mortality data.

claim: Most circadian cytokines show variable phase relations between free-running and entrained conditions.
source: Taken together, cytokine profiles of LPS-challenged mice parallel endotoxic shock-induced mortality patterns, although most circadian cytokines show variable phase relations between free-running and entrained conditions (Figure 1E).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: IFNγ, MCP-1, IL-6 and the anti-inflammatory cytokine IL-10 showed significantly altered levels between mice kept in LD or DD when injected at ZT8/CT8 with the same dose of LPS (13 mg/kg).
source: IFNγ, MCP-1, IL-6 and the anti-inflammatory cytokine IL-10 showed significantly altered levels between mice kept in LD or DD (Figure 1F), suggesting that in DD conditions the sensitivity to endotoxin is increased leading to enhanced pro-inflammatory cytokine secretion and subsequently increased mortality.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1F.

claim: In DD conditions the sensitivity to endotoxin is increased leading to enhanced pro-inflammatory cytokine secretion and subsequently increased mortality.
source: IFNγ, MCP-1, IL-6 and the anti-inflammatory cytokine IL-10 showed significantly altered levels between mice kept in LD or DD (Figure 1F), suggesting that in DD conditions the sensitivity to endotoxin is increased leading to enhanced pro-inflammatory cytokine secretion and subsequently increased mortality.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation of increased cytokine levels and mortality in DD conditions.

claim: Local clocks are thought to play important roles in mediating circadian modulation of cell- and tissue-specific functions.
source: Local clocks are thought to play important roles in mediating circadian modulation of cell- and tissue-specific functions (Stratmann and Schibler, 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: Depletion of local immune clocks has been shown to disrupt circadian patterns of tissue function.
source: In fact, depletion of local immune clocks has been shown to disrupt circadian patterns of tissue function (Nguyen et al., 2013; Curtis et al., 2015; Gibbs et al., 2012; Gibbs et al., 2014; Druzd et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: Mortality of myBmal-KO mice was still dependent on circadian time of LPS administration.
source: To our surprise, mortality of these mice was still dependent on circadian time of LPS administration (Figure 2A) indicating that a functional circadian clock in myeloid cells is not required for time-of-day-dependent LPS-sensitivity.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: A functional circadian clock in myeloid cells is not required for time-of-day-dependent LPS-sensitivity.
source: To our surprise, mortality of these mice was still dependent on circadian time of LPS administration (Figure 2A) indicating that a functional circadian clock in myeloid cells is not required for time-of-day-dependent LPS-sensitivity.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation of circadian mortality patterns in myBmal-KO mice.

claim: The overall susceptibility to LPS decreased twofold in myBmal-KO mice compared to wild-type mice.
source: However, the overall susceptibility to LPS decreased twofold compared to wild-type mice (Figure 2B,C and Figure 2—figure supplement 1E) suggesting that BMAL1 levels in myeloid cells directly or indirectly modulate susceptibility toward LPS.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B and 2C.

claim: BMAL1 levels in myeloid cells directly or indirectly modulate susceptibility toward LPS.
source: However, the overall susceptibility to LPS decreased twofold compared to wild-type mice (Figure 2B,C and Figure 2—figure supplement 1E) suggesting that BMAL1 levels in myeloid cells directly or indirectly modulate susceptibility toward LPS.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation of decreased susceptibility in myBmal-KO mice.

claim: The decreased susceptibility to LPS in myBmal-KO mice could only in part be attributed to genetic background.
source: The latter effect could only in part be attributed to genetic background (note decreased susceptibility to LPS in Lyz2 cre/cre) (hereafter called LysM-Cre) control mice (Figure 2C and Figure 2—figure supplement 1D) together arguing for a tonic rather than temporal role of myeloid BMAL1 in regulating LPS sensitivity.
evidence: This is supported by comparison of myBmal-KO and LysM-Cre control mice shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Myeloid BMAL1 has a tonic rather than temporal role in regulating LPS sensitivity.
source: The latter effect could only in part be attributed to genetic background (note decreased susceptibility to LPS in Lyz2 cre/cre) (hereafter called LysM-Cre) control mice (Figure 2C and Figure 2—figure supplement 1D) together arguing for a tonic rather than temporal role of myeloid BMAL1 in regulating LPS sensitivity.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that myBmal-KO mice show decreased overall susceptibility but maintained circadian patterns.

claim: Switching light conditions from LD to DD in myBmal-KO increased sensitivity to LPS similar to wild-type mice.
source: Furthermore, switching light conditions from LD to DD in myBmal-KO increased sensitivity to LPS similar to wild-type mice (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: BMAL1 has been linked with a number of other non-rhythmic processes such as adipogenesis, sleep regulation, and cartilage homeostasis.
source: Despite its essential role for circadian clock function, BMAL1 has been linked with a number of other non-rhythmic processes such as adipogenesis (Shimba et al., 2005), sleep regulation (Ehlen et al., 2017), and cartilage homeostasis (Dudek et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: CLOCK, like its heterodimeric binding partner BMAL1, has been shown to be an indispensable factor for peripheral clock function.
source: CLOCK, like its heterodimeric binding partner BMAL1, has also been shown to be an indispensable factor for peripheral clock function (DeBruyne et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: The expression of Clock mRNA and protein was substantially reduced in peritoneal cavity cells but was normal in liver of myClock-KO mice.
source: As expected, the expression of Clock mRNA and protein was substantially reduced in peritoneal cavity cells but was normal in liver (Figure 3A,B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A and 3B.

claim: Rhythmicity of Bmal1, Cry1, Cry2, Dbp, Npas2, and Nr1d1 mRNA levels was essentially eliminated in myClock-KO peritoneal macrophages.
source: Rhythmicity of Bmal1, Cry1, Cry2, Dbp, Npas2, and Nr1d1 mRNA levels was essentially eliminated, while a low amplitude rhythmicity was detected for Per1 and Per2 mRNA (Figure 3C,D and Figure 3—figure supplement 1D,E).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3C and 3D.

claim: A low amplitude rhythmicity was detected for Per1 and Per2 mRNA in myClock-KO peritoneal macrophages.
source: Rhythmicity of Bmal1, Cry1, Cry2, Dbp, Npas2, and Nr1d1 mRNA levels was essentially eliminated, while a low amplitude rhythmicity was detected for Per1 and Per2 mRNA (Figure 3C,D and Figure 3—figure supplement 1D,E).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3C and 3D.

claim: Circadian oscillations were disrupted in peritoneal cavity cells from myClock-KO mice.
source: Moreover, circadian oscillations were disrupted in peritoneal cavity cells (mainly macrophages and B-cells) from myClock-KO mice, but not in tissue explants from SCN or lung (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is supported by bioluminescence recording data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: Circadian oscillations were not disrupted in tissue explants from SCN or lung of myClock-KO mice.
source: Moreover, circadian oscillations were disrupted in peritoneal cavity cells (mainly macrophages and B-cells) from myClock-KO mice, but not in tissue explants from SCN or lung (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is supported by bioluminescence recording data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: Mortality in myClock-KO mice was significantly time-of-day dependent.
source: Again, mortality in these mice was significantly time-of-day dependent (Figure 3F).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3F.

claim: myClock-KO mice showed strongly reduced susceptibility to LPS compared to wild-type and to a lower degree to LysM-Cre control mice.
source: As in myBmal1-KO mice, myClock-KO mice showed strongly reduced susceptibility to LPS compared to wild-type and to a lower degree to LysM-Cre control mice (Figure 3G and Figure 3—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3G.

claim: Myeloid clockwork are dispensable for the time-of-day dependency in endotoxic shock.
source: Taken together, our data unequivocally show that myeloid clockwork are dispensable for the time-of-day dependency in endotoxic shock.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation of circadian mortality patterns in both myBmal-KO and myClock-KO mice.

claim: Myeloid CLOCK/BMAL1 has a non-temporal, sensitizing role in the regulation of endotoxic shock.
source: In addition, decreased overall susceptibility suggest a non-temporal, sensitizing role of myeloid CLOCK/BMAL1 in the regulation of endotoxic shock.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation of decreased overall susceptibility in both knockout strains.

claim: Cytokine levels in plasma collected 2 hr after LPS administration still exhibited circadian patterns for TNFα, IL-18, IL-10 in myClock-KO mice (p-values=0.046, 0.001 and 0.009, respectively).
source: Unexpectedly, cytokine levels in plasma, collected 2 hr after LPS administration still exhibited circadian patterns for TNFα, IL-18, IL-10 (Figure 4A) (p-values=0.046, 0.001 and 0.009, respectively), very similar to those observed in wild-type animals (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Circadian patterns of TNFα, IL-18, IL-10 in myClock-KO mice were very similar to those observed in wild-type animals.
source: Unexpectedly, cytokine levels in plasma, collected 2 hr after LPS administration still exhibited circadian patterns for TNFα, IL-18, IL-10 (Figure 4A) (p-values=0.046, 0.001 and 0.009, respectively), very similar to those observed in wild-type animals (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is supported by comparison of data shown in Figure 4A and 4B.

claim: An LPS-induced circadian cytokine response does not depend on a functional circadian clock in cells of myeloid origin.
source: These data suggest that an LPS-induced circadian cytokine response does not depend on a functional circadian clock in cells of myeloid origin.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation of circadian cytokine patterns in myClock-KO mice.

claim: Circadian cytokine expression might still be responsible for time-of-day-dependent mortality in endotoxic shock.
source: Thus, circadian cytokine expression might still be responsible for time-of-day-dependent mortality in endotoxic shock.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the findings.

claim: Levels of CCL7, MCP-1 and TNFα showed strong positive correlation with mortality (p-values=0.0003, 0.0065, 0.0319, respectively).
source: Levels of CCL7, MCP-1 and TNFα showed strong positive correlation with mortality (p-values=0.0003, 0.0065, 0.0319, respectively).
evidence: This is supported by correlation analysis shown in Figure 4C.

claim: IL-10 and IL-18 correlated negatively with mortality (p-values=0.0054 and 0.0004, respectively).
source: Others, such as IL-10 and IL-18 correlated negatively (p-values=0.0054 and 0.0004, respectively) (Figure 4C and Figure 4—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is supported by correlation analysis shown in Figure 4C.

claim: TNFα and IL-10 are well-known factors in the pathomechanism of endotoxic shock.
source: Interestingly, while TNFα and IL-10 are well-known factors in the pathomechanism of endotoxic shock, CCL7, MCP-1 and protective effects of IL-18 have not been reported in this context.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge from prior literature.

claim: CCL7, MCP-1 and protective effects of IL-18 have not been reported in the context of endotoxic shock.
source: Interestingly, while TNFα and IL-10 are well-known factors in the pathomechanism of endotoxic shock, CCL7, MCP-1 and protective effects of IL-18 have not been reported in this context.
evidence: This is based on review of prior literature.

claim: Local circadian clocks in myeloid lineage cells are dispensable for time-of-day-dependent plasma cytokine levels upon LPS challenge.
source: Together, our data suggest that local circadian clocks in myeloid lineage cells are dispensable for time-of-day-dependent plasma cytokine levels upon LPS challenge.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation of circadian cytokine patterns in myClock-KO mice.

claim: Circadian patterns in immune cell trafficking and distribution have been recently reported and linked to disease models and immune functions.
source: Circadian patterns in immune cell trafficking and distribution have been recently reported and linked to disease models and immune functions (Keller et al., 2009; Nguyen et al., 2013; Druzd et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: Homing and release/egress of hematopoetic stem cells (HSPCs), granulocytes, and lymphocytes to bone marrow and lymph nodes have been shown to vary in a time-of-day-dependent manner requiring the integrity of an immune-cell intrinsic circadian clock.
source: Similarly, homing and release/egress of hematopoetic stem cells (HSPCs), granulocytes, and lymphocytes to bone marrow and lymph nodes, respectively, have been shown to vary in a time-of-day-dependent manner requiring the integrity of an immune-cell intrinsic circadian clock (Druzd et al., 2017; Méndez-Ferrer et al., 2008; Scheiermann et al., 2012; Casanova-Acebes et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: The number of cells were significantly time-of-day dependent in bone marrow, spleen, and inguinal lymph nodes of wild-type mice.
source: As expected from previous studies (Druzd et al., 2017; Keller et al., 2009; Scheiermann et al., 2012) the number of cells were significantly time-of-day dependent in bone marrow, spleen, and inguinal lymph nodes of wild-type mice (Figure 5B, Figure 5—figure supplements 7–10).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: In spleen, F4/80+ macrophages of both myeloid clock knockout strains were still found at higher numbers at CT8 compared to CT20.
source: While in spleen, F4/80+ macrophages of both myeloid clock knockout strains were still found at higher numbers at CT8 compared to CT20 (Figure 5C), significant time-of-day differences of monocyte/macrophage numbers in wild-type blood diminished in myeloid clock knockouts (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Significant time-of-day differences of monocyte/macrophage numbers in wild-type blood diminished in myeloid clock knockouts.
source: While in spleen, F4/80+ macrophages of both myeloid clock knockout strains were still found at higher numbers at CT8 compared to CT20 (Figure 5C), significant time-of-day differences of monocyte/macrophage numbers in wild-type blood diminished in myeloid clock knockouts (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: There is a rather complex than mono-causal relation between myeloid clocks, circadian traffic and mortality risk in endotoxic shock.
source: Different patterns of time-of-day dependency were also observed in bone marrow (Figure 5E), together suggesting a rather complex than mono-causal relation between myeloid clocks, circadian traffic and mortality risk in endotoxic shock (for a comprehensive analysis of this dataset see Figure 5—figure supplements 7–10).
evidence: This is inferred from the complex patterns observed in immune cell trafficking data.

claim: Monocytes/macrophages have been identified as important cellular entities relaying the endotoxin (LPS) triggered signal to the immune system and other organ systems by means of massive secretion of pro-inflammatory cytokines.
source: First, monocytes/macrophages have been identified as important cellular entities relaying the endotoxin (LPS) triggered signal to the immune system and other organ systems by means of massive secretion of pro-inflammatory cytokines (Sabroe et al., 2002; Novick et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: A high amplitude circadian clock in monocytes/macrophages has been shown to control circadian cytokine output in vitro and ex vivo.
source: Second, a high amplitude circadian clock in monocytes/macrophages has been shown to control circadian cytokine output in vitro and ex vivo (Keller et al., 2009; Curtis et al., 2015; Bellet et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: A high amplitude time-of-day-dependent mortality has been demonstrated in endotoxic shock.
source: Third, a high amplitude time-of-day-dependent mortality has been demonstrated in endotoxic shock (Halberg et al., 1960).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: A cecal ligation and puncture model demonstrated loss of time-of-day dependency of mortality in myeloid Bmal1 knockout mice.
source: Fourth, a number of experiments done at two circadian time points, including a cecal ligation and puncture model (Deng et al., 2018), demonstrating loss of time-of-day dependency of mortality in myeloid Bmal1 knockout mice (Curtis et al., 2015) further supported this hypothesis.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Marpegan and colleagues reported that mice challenged with LPS at two different time points in constant darkness did not exhibit differences in mortality rates.
source: On the other hand, some studies suggested other mechanisms, for example Marpegan and colleagues reported that mice challenged with LPS at two different time points in constant darkness did not exhibit differences in mortality rates (Marpegan et al., 2009), arguing for a light-driven process in regulating time-of-day dependency in endotoxic shock.
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: The result from Marpegan et al. may be caused by a ceiling effect induced by constant darkness, since mortality rates at both time points were close to 100 percent.
source: However, we suspected that this result may be caused by a ceiling effect induced by constant darkness, since mortality rates at both time points were close to 100 percent.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of prior findings.

claim: Depletion/mutation of Per2 rendered mice insensitive to experimental time dependency in endotoxic shock.
source: Similarly, depletion/mutation of Per2 rendered mice insensitive to experimental time dependency in endotoxic shock (Liu et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: Depletion of either CLOCK or BMAL1 in myeloid lineage derived cells both did not abolish time-of-day dependency in mortality to endotoxic shock.
source: Surprisingly, however, we found that depletion of either CLOCK or BMAL1 in myeloid lineage derived cells both did not abolish time-of-day dependency in mortality to endotoxic shock, which led us to reject our initial hypothesis.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from myClock-KO and myBmal-KO mice.

claim: Data exclude light as a stimulus driving mortality in endotoxic shock.
source: Our data also exclude light as a stimulus driving mortality: First, data from Halberg, Marpegan, Scheiermann as well as our own lab (Halberg et al., 1960; Marpegan et al., 2009; Keller et al., 2009; Scheiermann et al., 2012) suggest that mice are more susceptible to endotoxic shock during the light phase compared to dark phase - whereas switching light schedules from light-dark to constant darkness led to an increase in overall mortality.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that DD increases overall mortality rather than eliminating circadian patterns.

claim: Mice are more susceptible to endotoxic shock during the light phase compared to dark phase.
source: Our data also exclude light as a stimulus driving mortality: First, data from Halberg, Marpegan, Scheiermann as well as our own lab (Halberg et al., 1960; Marpegan et al., 2009; Keller et al., 2009; Scheiermann et al., 2012) suggest that mice are more susceptible to endotoxic shock during the light phase compared to dark phase - whereas switching light schedules from light-dark to constant darkness led to an increase in overall mortality.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature and experimental data.

claim: Switching light schedules from light-dark to constant darkness led to an increase in overall mortality.
source: Our data also exclude light as a stimulus driving mortality: First, data from Halberg, Marpegan, Scheiermann as well as our own lab (Halberg et al., 1960; Marpegan et al., 2009; Keller et al., 2009; Scheiermann et al., 2012) suggest that mice are more susceptible to endotoxic shock during the light phase compared to dark phase - whereas switching light schedules from light-dark to constant darkness led to an increase in overall mortality.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1.

claim: Data unequivocally demonstrate circadian mortality rhythms upon LPS challenge even under DD conditions, irrespective of the genetic clock-gene depletion tested.
source: Second, irrespective of the genetic clock-gene depletion tested, our data unequivocally demonstrate circadian mortality rhythms upon LPS challenge even under DD conditions.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from wild-type, myBmal-KO, and myClock-KO mice in DD.

claim: Peripheral blood cytokine levels showed - though altered - circadian time dependency in the myClock-KO strain.
source: Strikingly, peripheral blood cytokine levels showed - though altered - circadian time dependency in the myClock-KO strain.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4.

claim: A burst of cytokines, following a lethal dose of LPS is generally thought to be an indispensable factor causing multi-organ dysfunction and leading to death.
source: A burst of cytokines, following a lethal dose of LPS is generally thought to be an indispensable factor causing multi-organ dysfunction and leading to death.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge about sepsis pathophysiology.

claim: The contribution of single cytokines has been difficult to tease apart due to complex nature of interconnected feedback systems.
source: However, the contribution of single cytokines has been difficult to tease apart due to complex nature of interconnected feedback systems.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge about cytokine networks.

claim: The pro-inflammatory cytokine TNFα was confirmed to act detrimentally in endotoxic shock.
source: While the pro-inflammatory cytokine TNFα was confirmed to act detrimentally, IL-18 surprisingly turned out to likely be protective.
evidence: This is supported by correlation analysis shown in Figure 4C.

claim: IL-18 surprisingly turned out to likely be protective in endotoxic shock.
source: While the pro-inflammatory cytokine TNFα was confirmed to act detrimentally, IL-18 surprisingly turned out to likely be protective.
evidence: This is supported by correlation analysis shown in Figure 4C.

claim: The protective role for IL-18 is supported by the negative correlation of IL-18 levels in blood and mortality risk.
source: This interpretation is not only supported by the negative correlation of IL-18 levels in blood and mortality risk, but also by an anti-phasic oscillation of IL-18 levels paralleling those of the known protective cytokine IL-10.
evidence: This is supported by correlation analysis shown in Figure 4C.

claim: IL-18 levels show an anti-phasic oscillation paralleling those of the known protective cytokine IL-10.
source: This interpretation is not only supported by the negative correlation of IL-18 levels in blood and mortality risk, but also by an anti-phasic oscillation of IL-18 levels paralleling those of the known protective cytokine IL-10.
evidence: This is inferred from the phase relationships shown in Figure 1E.

claim: A protective role for IL-18 has been previously reported in a colitis model in mice.
source: In addition, a protective role for IL-18 has been previously reported in a colitis model in mice (Dinarello et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: Circadian regulation of trafficking lymphocytes by cell intrinsic clockworks have been demonstrated to impact the pathophysiology of an autoimmune disease model such as EAE.
source: While circadian regulation of trafficking lymphocytes by cell intrinsic clockworks have been demonstrated to impact the pathophysiology of an autoimmune disease model such as EAE (Druzd et al., 2017), our data on distribution patterns of immune cells at two circadian time points draw a more complex picture.
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: In spleen, absolute numbers of macrophages, but not neutrophils and monocytes, are independent of their local clocks.
source: In spleen, absolute numbers of macrophages, but not neutrophils and monocytes, are independent of their local clocks.
evidence: This is inferred from the data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Patterns of macrophages and neutrophils in peripheral blood and bone marrow (respectively) change upon local myeloid clock depletion.
source: In contrast, patterns of macrophages and neutrophils in peripheral blood and bone marrow (respectively) change upon local myeloid clock depletion.
evidence: This is inferred from the data shown in Figure 5D and 5E.

claim: Myeloid cell traffic is regulated at multiple levels including cell-intrinsic, endothelial and site specific factors.
source: Thus, it appears that myeloid cell traffic is regulated at multiple levels including cell-intrinsic, endothelial and site specific factors.
evidence: This is inferred from the complex patterns observed in immune cell trafficking data.

claim: Data do not support the hypothesis of myeloid cell distribution being a main factor for time-of-day-dependent mortality risk in endotoxic shock.
source: However, our data do not support the hypothesis of myeloid cell distribution being a main factor for time-of-day-dependent mortality risk in endotoxic shock.
evidence: This is inferred from the complex and inconsistent patterns observed in immune cell trafficking data.

claim: The bio-availability of bacterial endotoxin injected intraperitoneally depends on multiple factors (i.e. pharmaco-kinetics), many of which themselves might underlie circadian regulation.
source: Following the pathophysiology of endotoxic shock on its path from cause to effect, it is important to note that the bio-availability of bacterial endotoxin injected intraperitoneally depends on multiple factors (i.e. pharmaco-kinetics), many of which themselves might underlie circadian regulation.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation based on knowledge of pharmacokinetics.

claim: Same doses of LPS administered i.p. at different times-of-day might result in highly diverging concentrations at the site of action.
source: As a consequence, same doses of LPS administered i.p. at different times-of-day might result in highly diverging concentrations at the site of action.
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on the possibility of circadian pharmacokinetics.

claim: Sensing of LPS by TLR4 is not restricted to myeloid lineage cells.
source: Sensing of LPS by TLR4 is not restricted to myeloid lineage cells (Hotchkiss et al., 2016; Wang et al., 2011; Bès-Houtmann et al., 2007; Abreu et al., 2002; Kato et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: Peritoneal mesothelial cells, adipocytes and adjacent organs might directly react to LPS and shape the complex response not only of cytokine release, but also in changing their metabolic states and tissue functions.
source: Subsequent to i.p. injection, peritoneal mesothelial cells, adipocytes and adjacent organs might directly react to LPS and shape the complex response not only of cytokine release, but also in changing their metabolic states and tissue functions.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation based on knowledge of LPS sensing.

claim: A recent study performed in a humanized mouse model identified non-hematopoetic derived cells as major source of many plasma cytokines after cecal ligation and puncture.
source: Indeed, a recent study performed in a humanized mouse model identified non-hematopoetic derived cells as major source of many plasma cytokines after cecal ligation and puncture (Skirecki et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: Local circadian clocks of non-hematopoietic cells may contribute to the time-of-day dependent cytokine patterns and survival observed in myeloid clock knockout mice.
source: Local circadian clocks of these cells may therefore contribute to the time-of-day dependent cytokine patterns and survival observed in myeloid clock knockout mice.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the findings.

claim: Rhythmic feeding behavior driven by the central pacemaker was suggested to alter immune-responses directly or indirectly.
source: Along this path, rhythmic feeding behavior driven by the central pacemaker was suggested to alter immune-responses directly or indirectly (Luna-Moreno et al., 2009; Laermans et al., 2014) and a recent study showed that day-time restricted feeding can reverse time-of-day dependent mortality rates (Geiger et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: Day-time restricted feeding can reverse time-of-day dependent mortality rates.
source: Along this path, rhythmic feeding behavior driven by the central pacemaker was suggested to alter immune-responses directly or indirectly (Luna-Moreno et al., 2009; Laermans et al., 2014) and a recent study showed that day-time restricted feeding can reverse time-of-day dependent mortality rates (Geiger et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: Nutrition-related factors could drive immune cells to respond differently to stimuli independent or dependent of local clocks.
source: Also, nutrition-related factors could drive immune cells to respond differently to stimuli independent or dependent of local clocks (Nguyen et al., 2013; Huang et al., 2007; Geiger et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior literature.

claim: The ability of cells and organs to resist all sorts of noxa might be regulated in a time-of-day-dependent manner.
source: Finally, the ability of cells and organs to resist all sorts of noxa might as well be regulated in a time-of-day-dependent manner.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation.

claim: Work from Hrushesky et al., 1994 showed that mice challenged with same doses of TNFα at various times throughout the day exhibited time-dependent survival paralleling phenomena in endotoxic shock.
source: Indeed, work from Hrushesky et al., 1994 showed that mice challenged with same doses of TNFα at various times throughout the day exhibited time-dependent survival paralleling phenomena in endotoxic shock.
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: Data showing fluctuating cytokine levels in myClock-KO mice challenged with LPS in constant darkness question the mechanism of organ vulnerability as the only source of circadian regulation.
source: However, our data showing fluctuating cytokine levels in myClock-KO mice challenged with LPS in constant darkness (Figure 4A) question the mechanism of organ vulnerability as the only source of circadian regulation.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation of circadian cytokine patterns in myClock-KO mice.

claim: Local myeloid clocks do not account for time-of-day dependent mortality in endotoxic shock.
source: While our work suggests that local myeloid clocks do not account for time-of-day dependent mortality in endotoxic shock it unequivocally argues for a strong enhancing effect of myeloid CLOCK and BMAL1 on overall susceptibility, which adds on the effect of light conditions.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation of circadian mortality patterns in myeloid clock knockout mice.

claim: Myeloid CLOCK and BMAL1 have a strong enhancing effect on overall susceptibility to LPS.
source: While our work suggests that local myeloid clocks do not account for time-of-day dependent mortality in endotoxic shock it unequivocally argues for a strong enhancing effect of myeloid CLOCK and BMAL1 on overall susceptibility, which adds on the effect of light conditions.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation of decreased overall susceptibility in myeloid clock knockout mice.

claim: The effect of myeloid CLOCK and BMAL1 on overall susceptibility adds on the effect of light conditions.
source: While our work suggests that local myeloid clocks do not account for time-of-day dependent mortality in endotoxic shock it unequivocally argues for a strong enhancing effect of myeloid CLOCK and BMAL1 on overall susceptibility, which adds on the effect of light conditions.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that both light conditions and myeloid clock genes affect overall susceptibility.

claim: Data stay in conflict with findings from other labs which rather reported attenuating effects of BMAL1 on inflammation.
source: However, it is important to note that our data do stay in conflict with findings from other labs which rather reported attenuating effects of BMAL1 on inflammation (Curtis et al., 2015; Nguyen et al., 2013; Deng et al., 2018) but align well with a report on clock mutant mice (Bellet et al., 2013).
evidence: This is based on comparison with prior literature.

claim: Data align well with a report on clock mutant mice.
source: However, it is important to note that our data do stay in conflict with findings from other labs which rather reported attenuating effects of BMAL1 on inflammation (Curtis et al., 2015; Nguyen et al., 2013; Deng et al., 2018) but align well with a report on clock mutant mice (Bellet et al., 2013).
evidence: This is based on comparison with prior literature.

claim: Differences in genetic background of mouse strains, animal-facility-dependent microbiomes or animal care procedures might account for differences with other studies.
source: Differences in genetic background of mouse strains, animal-facility-dependent microbiomes (Sanz and Moya-Pérez, 2014) or animal care procedures might account for this but remain unsatisfying explanations.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of discrepancies with prior literature.

claim: One of the most striking findings is the large increase in susceptibility to endotoxic shock when mice were housed under DD as compared to LD conditions.
source: One of the most striking findings of our work is the large increase in susceptibility to endotoxic shock when mice were housed under DD as compared to LD conditions.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1.

claim: The relative increase in susceptibility when shifting from LD to DD was observed in wild-type as well as in myBmal-KO mice and appears therefore independent of a functional clock in myeloid cells.
source: This relative increase when shifting from LD to DD was observed in wild-type as well as in myBmal-KO mice and appears therefore independent of a functional clock in myeloid cells.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Carlson and Chiu reported similar effects in a cecal ligation and puncture model in rats upon transfer to LL (constant light) or DD conditions, where they found decreased survival as compared to rats remaining in LD conditions.
source: Interestingly, Carlson and Chiu reported similar effects in a cecal ligation and puncture model in rats upon transfer to LL (constant light) or DD conditions, where they found decreased survival as compared to rats remaining in LD conditions (Carlson and Chiu, 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior literature.

claim: Rhythmic light conditions, rather than light itself promote survival in endotoxemia.
source: It is tempting to speculate that rhythmic light conditions, rather than light itself promote survival in endotoxemia.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the findings.

claim: It will be important to further investigate these phenomena not only in respect to animal housing conditions, which need to be tightly light controlled in immunological, physiological, and behavioral experiments but also for their apparent implications on health-care in intensive care units.
source: In either case, it will be important to further investigate these phenomena not only in respect to animal housing conditions, which need to be tightly light controlled in immunological, physiological, and behavioral experiments but also for their apparent implications on health-care in intensive care units.
